entities.summary:
Elle, founded in 1945 by Hélène Gordon-Lazareff, is a French weekly lifestyle magazine that has become a hallmark of modern media. Published in Paris, it has significantly influenced global fashion and lifestyle trends, reflecting the evolving roles of women in society post-World War II. The magazine not only catered to the burgeoning consumerism of the era but also positioned itself as a platform for female empowerment and expression, making it an essential part of contemporary cultural history.

Since its inception, Elle has covered various topics including fashion, beauty, health, and culture, shaping public perceptions and tastes. The magazine has a unique blend of editorial content and advertising, reaching millions of readers worldwide. It has expanded internationally, with editions in multiple languages, thus playing a crucial role in disseminating French fashion and lifestyle ideals globally. The annual Elle Style Awards, established in 1994, further cemented its influence in the fashion industry, recognizing outstanding contributions and trends.

Elle’s legacy is profound; it has not only transformed the publishing landscape but has also influenced the dialogue surrounding women's issues. The magazine has served as a catalyst for discussions on body positivity, diversity, and representation within the fashion industry. Its impact continues to resonate, inspiring new generations of readers and writers while shaping the contours of lifestyle journalism.
